correctness.rationale: Reconstructed the smooth three-dimensional relative-phase ODE from the four sine-coupled equations. Logarithmic derivatives of J_u and J_v cancel identically against the reduced vector field; an independent SymPy implementation confirms this identity for general tangent parameter. On the balanced slice their squared-sine profiles have maxima rho^2 cos(alpha) exp(alpha tan(alpha)), giving the unique sharp threshold. Below threshold, cos u and cos v remain positive and delta decreases to zero; at the double envelope root, uniqueness prevents finite-time saddle arrival. Above threshold, simple envelope crossings glue four regular sign branches into a compact circle with nonvanishing vector field, yielding relative periodicity and the convergent endpoint-square-root quadrature. The argument excludes endpoint alpha,rho and common-phase periodicity.
correctness.risk: One-dimensional balanced slice only; a given common-phase lift need not be periodic. Near separatrix numerical approach cannot certify the infinite-time equality trajectory.
